court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Standard of review of agency findings
issues.why: The court must apply substantial evidence for factual findings and de novo for legal questions.

issues.label: Adverse credibility determination validity
issues.why: The court must assess whether the four grounds for the adverse credibility finding are supported by specific, cogent, record-based reasons.

issues.label: Specificity of each credibility ground
issues.why: Each of the four distinct bases must be individually examined for record support.

issues.label: REAL ID Act totality-of-circumstances standard
issues.why: Credibility findings must account for the totality of circumstances and all relevant factors.

issues.label: Whether inconsistencies go to heart of claim
issues.why: The court should evaluate whether cited discrepancies are material or trivial.

issues.label: Corroborating evidence sufficiency
issues.why: The IJ found corroboration did not rehabilitate testimony; the court must review that assessment.

issues.label: Notice and opportunity to provide corroboration
issues.why: The applicant may be entitled to notice before corroboration is required, especially proceeding pro se.

issues.label: Past persecution establishment
issues.why: The rally shooting, arrest, and torture may constitute past persecution triggering a presumption of future fear.

issues.label: Nexus to protected ground
issues.why: Harm must be on account of political opinion or membership in UNITA/opposition.

issues.label: Well-founded fear of future persecution
issues.why: The court must consider whether an objectively reasonable fear exists independent of past harm.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility and burden
issues.why: The court must assess whether relocation is reasonable and who bears the burden given possible past persecution.

issues.label: Reasonableness of relocation to Kanfufu/Luanda Norte
issues.why: Applicant continued hiding after relocating, raising doubt about safety of relocation.

issues.label: Government as persecutor and relocation
issues.why: When the persecutor is the government, the presumption against reasonable relocation applies.

issues.label: Withholding of removal higher standard
issues.why: Withholding requires a clear probability of persecution, requiring separate analysis.

issues.label: CAT claim independent of credibility
issues.why: CAT relief must be evaluated on all record evidence, not solely on discredited testimony.

issues.label: Country conditions evidence for CAT
issues.why: The court must consider objective country conditions demonstrating torture risk regardless of credibility.

issues.label: Particularized risk of torture standard
issues.why: CAT requires showing a specific likelihood the applicant would be tortured.

issues.label: Government acquiescence or involvement in torture
issues.why: CAT requires torture by or with consent/acquiescence of a public official.

issues.label: Whether agency improperly conflated credibility with CAT
issues.why: Denying CAT solely because testimony was not credible may be legal error.

issues.label: Due process claim standard
issues.why: The prejudice test asks whether the outcome may have been affected by the violation.

issues.label: Exhaustion of due process arguments
issues.why: Some due process arguments were not raised before the BIA, raising exhaustion/jurisdiction concerns.

issues.label: Pro se applicant fairness and hearing conduct
issues.why: Proceeding pro se may implicate the IJ's duty to develop the record fully.

issues.label: Derivative relief for family members
issues.why: The wife and family's status depends on the applicant's asylum or independent claims.

issues.label: Wife's non-testimony and rape/harm evidence
issues.why: The court may consider harm to the family and why the wife did not testify.

issues.label: Effect of threats and killing of neighbor
issues.why: Third-party harm to similarly situated persons supports future fear analysis.

issues.label: Cumulative effect of incidents as persecution
issues.why: Multiple beatings, detention, and torture must be assessed cumulatively.

issues.label: Timeliness of asylum application
issues.why: Though filed timely, the one-year deadline must be confirmed satisfied.

issues.label: Remand versus affirmance disposition
issues.why: The court must decide whether errors warrant remand or the record supports affirmance.
